payload.analysis: Belief plus records: marrow normocellular, mild megakaryocytic hyperplasia, no dysplasia, favoring reactive thrombocytosis over MPL/MPN. Recurrent PE on rivaroxaban, menorrhagia, Hb 6.6, iron deficiency and thrombocytosis best fit rivaroxaban-induced anemia. Missing menstrual history, vWF/platelet function, endoscopy and Hb response limit certainty; thrombophilia persists. Available evidence covered.

payload.report: The patient, a 19-year-old female on rivaroxaban for unprovoked PE, developed menorrhagia with hemoglobin dropping from 14.9 to 6.6 g/dL and ferritin 6.8 ng/mL (iron deficiency), requiring transfusion. Rising platelets (402→485→566) and marrow showing normocellularity with mild megakaryocytic hyperplasia and no dysplasia indicate reactive thrombocytosis, not marrow disease; negative JAK2/CALR/MPL weakens MPN. Thus the anemia best fits rivaroxaban-induced bleeding, with inherited thrombophilia a moderate consideration for recurrent PE.
